notes: SGLang's router is the routing layer for multi-model and data-parallel SGLang deployments. The data_parallel_controller.py implements four load balancing methods: ROUND_ROBIN (simple round-robin), FOLLOW_BOOTSTRAP_ROOM (route to the worker with the prefix cached), TOTAL_REQUESTS (route to the worker with the fewest requests), and TOTAL_TOKENS (route to the worker with the fewest total tokens). TOTAL_TOKENS is the most relevant for LLM serving because it is a proxy for KV cache pressure - a worker processing more tokens has less KV cache available. However, it is a proxy, not a direct measurement: it does not account for cache hits, and it does not account for the fact that a worker with many short requests may have more available cache than a worker with few long requests. The router is SGLang-specific and does not route to other engines. ||| MAINTENANCE (dated fact, GitHub API, 2026-10-04): last commit 2026-10-04 (0.0 months before this record), latest release v0.5.21 published 2026-10-02, 1996 contributors (distinct committers including anonymous), open_issues_count 5553 (issues PLUS pull requests - see [[ev-github-open-issues-count-includes-pull-requests]]), not archived, 36777 stars. UPDATED 2026-10-04 against the in-tree sgl-model-gateway README (dep-sgl-model-gateway-readme), which supersedes part of this record. The router has been generalised from a data-parallel controller into an explicit control plane plus data plane: control plane is the Worker Manager (validates workers, discovers capabilities, keeps the registry in sync), a Job Queue serialising add/remove with status at /workers/{worker_id}, a background health checker and load monitor, and optional Kubernetes service discovery; data plane is the HTTP/PD/gRPC/OpenAI routers plus a resilience layer (token-bucket rate limiting, request queuing, retry executor with default max 5 retries and exponential backoff triggered on 408/429/500/502/503/504, per-worker circuit breakers). Load-balancing policies are now enumerated: random, round_robin, cache_aware (a prefix tree of prompts with --cache-threshold, --balance-abs-threshold, --balance-rel-threshold, --eviction-interval, --max-tree-size), and power_of_two (lighter of two random candidates, integrated with LoadMonitor), with per-model overrides via --prefill-policy / --decode-policy in PD mode and via worker labels in IGW mode. Note what this does to the earlier FOLLOW_BOOTSTRAP_ROOM and TOTAL_TOKENS caveats: they are earlier-generation mechanisms that cache_aware and power_of_two supersede as the general path, though cache_aware carries the same class of staleness risk - see dep-kv-aware-router-view-cannot-be-rebuilt-after-restart for the upstream statement that the KV placement view cannot be rebuilt after a restart and degrades to worse routing rather than an error. Also newly documented: --enable-igw multi-model mode where workers are registered at runtime by POST /workers with url, model_id, priority and labels, which makes routing a mutable runtime API rather than static config.
